problems: Cliopatria 'British Gold Coast' (1873-1960) is a composite of the Gold Coast, Nigeria and the British Cameroons; the 1960 shape has no Ghana at all and the row outlives the colony (ends 6 March 1957) by three years. All shapes reviewed as adjust (1960 wrong). The orchestrator should not render the row's Nigerian cells as Gold Coast.

Cliopatria 'German Africa' starts 1871 (7-cell Douala patch) but German rule in Africa starts 1884; the kamerun dossier (another group) names german-africa as its successor in 1871. This dossier starts 1884-04 and ends 1919-06 (Treaty of Versailles), keeping the occupied colonies as German-owned land (hatched by the occupiers) from 1915 to 1919, per master-plan rule 4; siblings (south-africa 1920, british-africa 1919/1922, french-africa 1919/1922) date their gains later than the 28 June 1919 German end, and french-africa dates Neukamerun's return 1919 against the Agadir Crisis page's 1916.

british-togoland was written here as a direct counterpart (the brief allows counterparts no row covers); german-africa, british-gold-coast and the ghana dossier now point at it. If af-08-x writes a second British Togoland dossier under the same slug, merge them. The ghana dossier equates it with the Volta Region (101 cells) while this dossier uses 79 cells from Cliopatria's Togoland shape.
